rationale: Job asks whether the Lord hears the ungodly person's plea in distress. Elihu later speaks of oppressed people crying out and of cries not heard because of evil people's insolence. The comparison concerns the lack of a hearing without identifying the oppressed criers with the ungodly person in Job's question.

Job pictures his former roads and mountains flooded with butter and milk; Zophar had wished that the ungodly person not see the milking of herds or pastures of honey and butter. The figurative and stated details are preserved.
Job says God regards him as clay and describes his portion as earth and ashes; his earlier appeal recalled being molded as clay and turned back to earth.

relationship: Claiming attachment to God does not establish wisdom
rationale: Elihu warns the friends not to say that they found wisdom by attaching themselves to the Lord; Job had warned that attaching themselves to Him would not prevent divine reproof for partiality.

relationship: Shared drinking metaphor: mockery and injustice
rationale: Elihu pictures Job drinking mockery like water; Eliphaz had pictured an unclean man drinking injustice as a drink. The comparison concerns the drinking image and preserves its different objects; the following Job 34:8 says without sinning or acting ungodly, so drinking mockery is not silently treated as the same wrongdoing as drinking injustice.

The proposed appeal asks God to show the speaker and promises not to add to injustice if he practiced it; Job had asked to be taught his sins and lawless deeds. The comparison does not replace apart from myself I will see with a claim of not having seen.
